question: Why does a pure inductor act as a 'short circuit' (zero resistance path) when connected to a DC voltage source, but offers significant opposition when connected to an AC voltage source?

options.A: DC voltage is usually lower than AC voltage.
options.B: The back EMF, which opposes current flow, is only induced when the current is changing (AC), not when it is constant (DC).
options.C: The magnetic field in an inductor cannot form under DC conditions.
options.D: The resistance of the wire of the inductor becomes zero only when DC flows through it.
